stages.title: See what Leave No Trace does and how a round plays

screens.title: Look at a round of Leave No Trace, from Start walking to the score

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how a round of Leave No Trace plays and how it scores.
Leave No Trace is an arcade game that you play with the keyboard. It is on Slieve Meelmore, the third place on the Summit Ready map.
You build one game from each pair of game chapters. Leave No Trace is paired with Whiteout, so you build one of those two.
First you build Leave No Trace exactly as it is in Summit Ready. Then, in stage 5, you change it into an arcade game on your own topic.
A round starts in a green field on the hill. Your own avatar stands at the left. 8 pieces of litter lie at random places, and 3 sheep wander about.

screenshot.alt: Leave No Trace before the round starts, with the avatar, the litter, the sheep and Start walking

marks.say: Your avatar: the picture you chose when you registered.
Start walking starts the round.
The dark strip shows the litter picked up and the time left.
The 3 hearts are your lives.
A sheep. Keep away from the sheep.
A piece of litter: an apple core.

screenshot.cap: Leave No Trace before you press Start walking.

blocks.p: You press **Start walking**. Then you walk your avatar with the arrow keys, or with W, A, S and D. Walking onto a piece of litter picks it up.
If a sheep touches you, it knocks you over and one heart turns grey. For 1.5 seconds after that, your avatar flashes and no sheep can knock you over again.
The round ends when you pick up all 8 pieces, when a sheep knocks you over 3 times, or when the 45 seconds run out.
Each piece of litter scores 10 points. If you pick up all 8, the seconds left are added on, up to 20 more. So all 8 with 30 seconds left scores 100 points, and 5 pieces scores 50 points.

blocks.p: Leave No Trace never crashes because of a missing picture or sound. This is what you see instead.
If `field.jpg` is missing, the field is plain light green.
If a litter picture or `sheep.png` is missing, that piece or that sheep is invisible, but it is still there. You can still pick up an invisible piece, and an invisible sheep can still knock you over.
If `icon-heart-64.png` is missing, no hearts show.
If a sound is missing, that moment is silent, and the game carries on.
To put a missing file back, you download the [[zip file|2]] again and paste its folders into bin\Debug. When Windows asks about the files you already have, you click **Skip these files**.
Skipping keeps every file you already have, including any file you changed. Only the missing files are copied in.

screens.title: Type PlaceLitter, which scatters 8 pieces of litter

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmLitter scatters 8 pieces of litter at random places in the field. None is right beside the avatar or under the dark strip.
A piece of litter right beside the start would be too easy, and one under the dark strip could not be seen. So the code picks a random place, and picks again until the place is fair.

code.title: PlaceLitter
code.why: You type the loop that finds a fair place, because it is new. The other lines make a PictureBox and set its properties, like the ones you set in stage 3. So they come in the copy.
partLines: The start point, and 8 turns
`start` is where the avatar stands. The `for` loop runs 8 times, once for each piece.
A new piece of litter
Each piece is a new PictureBox, 40 pixels square, with a Transparent background. `i % 7` is the remainder after dividing by 7, so the 8th piece uses the first picture again.
Get ready to look
`x` and `y` will hold the place. `tooClose` starts as true, so the loop below runs at least once.
A random place
`random.Next` gives a number by chance, anywhere across or down the field. The 40 keeps the whole piece inside the field.
How far from the start
`Math.Abs` gives the distance without a minus sign, so `across` and `down` say how far the place is from the start.
Under the dark strip
`underStrip` is true when the place is under the dark strip in the top right corner.
Fair or not
The place is too close when it is within 120 pixels of the start both across and down. It is unfair under the strip too. If so, the `while` loop goes round again and picks a new place.
Put the piece down
The piece goes to the fair place. It is kept in the `litter` array, and `pnlField.Controls.Add` puts it in the field.

partLines: The clock

glossary: How tall a control is, in pixels.
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.

A control that shows a picture. The avatar, each piece of litter, each sheep and each heart is a PictureBox.
A property of a form. When it is True, the form hears every key press first, before any control on it.
A property of a form. When it is True, the form draws each picture off the screen first, then shows it all at once, so nothing flickers.
The event that happens the moment a key is pressed down.
The event that happens the moment a key is let go.
Which key was pressed. `Keys.Up` is the up arrow, and `Keys.W` is the W key.
A value that is either true or false. `goUp` is a bool: true while the up arrow is held down.
A control that never shows on the window. Once started, it runs its Tick method every time its Interval runs out, until it is stopped.
How long a Timer waits before each Tick, in thousandths of a second. 20 means 0.02 seconds.
The event a Timer has. Its method runs every time the Timer's Interval runs out.
A Timer that runs every few thousandths of a second and moves everything a little each time. `tmrGame` is the game loop of Leave No Trace.
Gives numbers by chance. `random.Next(0, 10)` gives a whole number from 0 up to 9.
Gives a number without its minus sign. `Math.Abs(-5)` gives 5. It tells you how far apart two numbers are.
A place on a window or a panel: how far across, X, and how far down, Y.
The rectangle that a control fills on its panel: where it is, and how big.
Asks whether two rectangles overlap. It is true when the avatar touches a sheep or a piece of litter.
Whether a control shows. A control with Visible false is hidden.
Whether a control can be used. A button with Enabled false is greyed out, and clicking it does nothing.
`Color.Transparent` lets whatever is behind a control show through it.
`picPlayer.Top -= 6` takes 6 away from Top, so the avatar moves 6 pixels up. `+= 6` adds 6.
`%` gives what is left over after a division. `13 % 10` is 3.
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when every one of its parts is true.
`!` means not. `!goUp` is true when `goUp` is false.
`foreach` runs a loop once for each thing in an array, such as each sheep in `sheep`.
`while` runs a loop again and again, for as long as its test is true.
Puts a control in front of every other control on the same panel.
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.
